title: Change Ledger
user: Solo service freelancers who need a client to approve added or changed fixed-price scope before the work silently becomes unpaid.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A freelancer reports work scattered across Gmail, WhatsApp, payment links, and spreadsheets, with time and revenue lost to tool fragmentation.
An Invoice Ninja user asks to remove or raise the four-custom-field limit because invoices and bills need more workflow-specific information.

recurrence: Two 2025 reports from separate communities; scope facts are regularly buried in messaging and generic invoicing fields.
current_workaround: Email or WhatsApp threads, a revised PDF quote, and manually copying the approved delta into an invoice.
incumbents_and_gap: Bonsai, HoneyBook, and Invoice Ninja cover proposals or full CRM; none make a tiny, client-readable approved-change ledger the primary artifact between quote and invoice.
smallest_useful_product: Offline PWA with clients, a base quote, line-item change cards, an immutable approval link/receipt, and CSV/PDF export. Non-goals: payment processing, project management, or AI scope estimation.
success_measure: In a 60-day pilot, 70% of created change cards receive an explicit client decision before related work is marked done.
monetization: one-time — a local, occasional business-control utility should not add another subscription to a freelancer stack.
constraints: Approval receipts need timestamp and content hash; do not claim electronic-signature or legal enforceability; client data stays in the browser unless the owner exports it.
why_distinct: It is a narrow evidence trail for scope variation, not a generic proposal generator or CRM.

title: Quote Decision
user: Tiny agencies that need an internal approval checkpoint and a clear client decision trail for quotes before anyone sends or starts work.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A freelancer explicitly asks what invoicing features matter and what current tools get wrong or overcomplicate in real workflows.
A self-hosted Invoice Ninja user requests an approve-and-send/deny-sending workflow for draft quotes and invoices based on staff permissions.

recurrence: Current requests in 2025 and 2026 show that quote workflow is more than document generation; a missed review can become unprofitable committed work.
current_workaround: Slack/email sign-off, a shared spreadsheet column, and manually forwarding a PDF to the client.
incumbents_and_gap: PandaDoc, Qwilr, and Invoice Ninja offer document workflows, but are heavy for a two-person shop that only needs review, send, accept/decline, and a clean record.
smallest_useful_product: Local quote checklist with one reviewer, send-ready status, accept/decline page, expiry date, and signed decision export. Non-goals: e-signature compliance claims, payments, or document editor.
success_measure: At least 90% of pilot quotes have both a pre-send review status and a recorded client decision within 30 days.
monetization: one-time — it replaces a small but high-consequence coordination ritual without requiring hosted accounts.
constraints: Use explicit consent and preserve the exact accepted version; no legal claim that a click is a regulated signature; expose a data-export/delete control.
why_distinct: The value is a decision audit for very small teams, not prettier quote templates.

title: Delivery Receipt
user: Freelancers delivering files or completed services who need a neutral record of what was delivered, when, and whether the client accepted it before a payment dispute.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A freelancer describes unpaid work and a desire to avoid spending hours chasing payment after delivering files.
A service business asks for different late-fee schedules because some work is due monthly while other work is due immediately when rendered.

recurrence: Separate 2025–2026 requests connect completed work, due timing, and the uncomfortable manual chase after delivery.
current_workaround: Email attachments, cloud-drive share links, screenshots, and a manually written invoice reminder.
incumbents_and_gap: Dropbox, Google Drive, DocuSign, and invoice systems each retain a fragment; they do not create a lightweight delivery-to-acceptance receipt for ordinary freelance handoff.
smallest_useful_product: Local web app that hashes a selected file manifest or service checklist, creates a client acknowledgement page, records acknowledgement/decline and exports a receipt PDF. Non-goals: escrow, locking customer work, collections, or legal representation.
success_measure: In pilots, 75% of completed engagements have a delivery receipt sent before the final invoice due date.
monetization: one-time — this is an episodic risk-control record, not an ongoing payment service.
constraints: Never hold files, money, or credentials; disclose that the receipt is evidence only and legal effect depends on jurisdiction and contract.
why_distinct: It supports fair, documented handoff instead of a coercive paywall around client work.

title: Send-Date Ledger
user: Freelancers who draft an invoice while work evolves and need the issued date, due date, and sent version to remain unambiguous.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An invoicing-platform builder identifies freelancer frustration with forced payment methods and over-complicated small-business interfaces.
A user says invoices can be created weeks before send while work is added, and asks that the invoice date reflect sending rather than draft creation.

recurrence: A 2025 request for less-bloated freelancer invoicing and a concrete 2026 date-error request point to an avoidable record-keeping failure.
current_workaround: Edit dates by hand in an invoice app or duplicate a draft just before emailing it.
incumbents_and_gap: FreshBooks, Wave, and Invoice Ninja manage complete invoices, but draft-versus-issued chronology is rarely a small, visible, exportable control.
smallest_useful_product: Offline invoice issue register: import or enter a PDF/amount, record draft, issued, sent, due, and paid events, and export a monthly ledger. Non-goals: accounting ledger, tax calculation, or payment gateway.
success_measure: For a pilot month, 95% of issued invoices have a recorded sent date and a due date generated from a visible rule.
monetization: one-time — local audit hygiene is a focused utility rather than a financial SaaS suite.
constraints: Dates must be timezone-aware and immutable once exported; do not present the register as statutory bookkeeping; browser storage needs encrypted export option.
why_distinct: It is a chronology guardrail around existing invoices, not another invoice creator.

title: Invoice Packet
user: Cross-border freelancers and tiny firms who need to assemble the exact invoice, work proof, payment proof, and accountant notes requested for a filing or client review.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Freelancers earning internationally in India report that GST, TDS, FEMA filings, and CA coordination still mean spreadsheets, WhatsApp pings, and panic.
An e-invoice user asks to choose the attachments delivered with each invoice so the recipient receives the right supporting documents.

recurrence: The operational compliance burden appears both in freelancer reporting and in a current e-invoice attachment request; missing support can delay a filing or payment.
current_workaround: A folder per invoice, named PDFs, spreadsheets, and ad-hoc WhatsApp coordination with an accountant.
incumbents_and_gap: Zoho Books, QuickBooks, and Invoice Ninja attach documents, but a jurisdiction-neutral, local checklist that produces a shareable evidence packet is not their main workflow.
smallest_useful_product: Offline pack builder with configurable checklist templates, file hashes, missing-item flags, accountant notes, and ZIP/PDF manifest export. Non-goals: tax advice, filing submission, OCR extraction, or storing documents in a vendor cloud.
success_measure: In a pilot, 80% of selected invoices produce a complete packet on first accountant review, with no follow-up request for a listed item.
monetization: one-time — privacy-sensitive, seasonal compliance preparation is better aligned with ownership than monthly storage fees.
constraints: Templates must be clearly jurisdiction-configurable and not legal/tax advice; files remain local; support encrypted export and filename redaction.
why_distinct: It organizes evidence around one business event instead of trying to replace bookkeeping or a chartered accountant.

title: Gentle Nudge
user: Independent service providers who need to prepare consistent, escalating but human-approved payment reminders without delegating client relationships to an AI bot.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A small-business owner says at least one client misses payment each month and describes follow-up as awkward, needy, and mentally draining.
An active Invoice Ninja request asks for different automatic email templates for recurring customers, reflecting the need for context-specific payment communication.

recurrence: Monthly late-payment stress is explicit in 2025, while the still-active invoicing request shows that one generic automated message does not fit recurring client relationships.
current_workaround: Calendar reminders, copied email templates, and either avoiding follow-up or turning on impersonal automatic dunning.
incumbents_and_gap: QuickBooks, FreshBooks, Stripe, and Invoice Ninja offer reminders, but small operators need a private prepare-review-send cadence that preserves discretion and relationship context.
smallest_useful_product: Local PWA with invoice dates, editable stage templates, a due-today queue, client-specific pause notes, and copy/email-draft output. Non-goals: auto-sending, payment prediction, debt collection, or access to bank accounts.
success_measure: After 45 days, pilot users prepare a first reminder within two business days of due date for at least 80% of overdue invoices.
monetization: one-time — the product lowers emotional overhead without needing to sit in the middle of payments or email delivery.
constraints: No automated email, profiling, or collection threats; templates should be editable and jurisdiction-neutral; local data export/delete is mandatory.
why_distinct: It is a respectful human-in-the-loop reminder workspace, not a thin AI collections wrapper.

title: Billable Review
user: Freelancers using a separate timer and accounting tool who need to review unbilled time before it is lost or turned into the wrong invoice.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A Swiss SMB/freelancer workflow reports manually exporting time from Toggl or Clockify and creating Bexio invoices, costing 3–5 hours each month.
An Invoice Ninja user asks for a dashboard total of tasks that have not yet been invoiced.

recurrence: Two current requests identify the same handoff: billable work exists in one place while invoice status lives in another.
current_workaround: Export time CSVs, filter in a spreadsheet, then manually create line items and mark rows billed.
incumbents_and_gap: Toggl, Clockify, Harvest, Bexio, and Invoice Ninja offer broad time or invoicing products; the missing lightweight layer is a local, exception-first unbilled review.
smallest_useful_product: CSV-in, offline review board that groups entries by client/project/date, flags stale or uncategorized time, records a local invoice reference, and exports approved line items. Non-goals: timer, accounting sync, payroll, or invoice sending.
success_measure: Pilot users reconcile 90% of imported billable rows to an invoice reference or explicit write-off within one monthly close.
monetization: one-time — it works with existing tools and has periodic rather than daily value.
constraints: Import only user-selected CSV; preserve original rows; no credential-based integrations in v1; make rounding and write-offs explicit.
why_distinct: It is a cross-tool review step, not another time tracker or accounting package.

title: Private Intake
user: Small field-service teams that need a booking form to collect client details while ensuring assigned workers see only the information needed to do the job.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A small-business scheduling discussion calls out rigid availability, paywalled reminders, and an impersonal booking experience.
A team-booking user asks for admin-only fields because property, contact, site, project, and commercial details can otherwise be visible to assigned staff.

recurrence: Scheduling friction and a specific privacy request appear in separate current communities; excess access to client details is a meaningful operational risk.
current_workaround: Put sensitive context in a manager's notes, text workers separately, or accept that team-booking fields are broadly visible.
incumbents_and_gap: Calendly, Cal.com, Square Appointments, and Google Forms have booking or form features, but small teams need a simple role-specific job brief without adopting a full field-service suite.
smallest_useful_product: Hosted booking form and staff view with field-level roles (admin, assigned worker), a minimal job brief, redaction preview, and deletion date. Non-goals: calendar sync, payments, dispatch optimization, or customer CRM.
success_measure: In a pilot, 100% of configured private fields are absent from worker views while 90% of workers can open a complete permitted brief before an appointment.
monetization: subscription — controlled client access and expiring hosted forms require a reliable service boundary.
constraints: Field-level authorization must be server-enforced; minimize PII retention; support deletion/export and regional privacy notices; do not expose booking identifiers in logs.
why_distinct: It narrows booking software to least-privilege intake instead of competing as another calendar.

title: Capacity Map
user: Two-to-ten-person service businesses that need to express which jobs can overlap by staff member, service type, and shared resource without buying enterprise scheduling.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A freelancer says Calendly and SavvyCal become overkill for paid sessions, multiple meeting types, and client-friendly small-team booking.
A Cal.com request describes companies and clinics where overlapping availability is sensible only for particular service types or team members; it has 6 reactions and 14 comments.

recurrence: Two May 2025 discussions identify a precise small-team scheduling edge case rather than a need for another generic calendar.
current_workaround: Separate calendars, duplicate event types, manual availability blocks, or rejecting useful bookings to avoid accidental conflicts.
incumbents_and_gap: Calendly, Cal.com, Acuity, and Square Appointments support availability, but their configuration is often oriented around a user calendar rather than an explainable compatibility matrix for a tiny crew.
smallest_useful_product: Local planning PWA with staff, services, shared resources, overlap rules, and a visual what-can-book-now matrix. Non-goals: public booking page, payments, calendar sync, or route planning.
success_measure: Pilot businesses can model all their normal service-overlap rules in under 30 minutes and identify zero disallowed overlaps in a two-week schedule review.
monetization: one-time — capacity planning can be a local companion to an existing booking system.
constraints: Make precedence and conflicts explainable; no employee surveillance data; import/export CSV only in v1.
why_distinct: It makes conditional overlap understandable; it is not a booking link clone.

title: Continuity Pack
user: Small businesses using self-hosted or local admin software who need a tested, readable recovery pack for invoices, customers, and business records.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An Ask HN participant asks whether small and mid-market businesses want installable/local alternatives to subscription SaaS.
A self-hosted Invoice Ninja user asks to combine backup and scheduler facilities to regularly push recoverable backups to a chosen target.

recurrence: The current demand for local ownership is paired with a concrete request for regular backups; data recovery is a trust prerequisite, not an optional admin task.
current_workaround: Occasional database dump, a cloud-folder copy, or a hosting-provider backup with no documented restore check.
incumbents_and_gap: Restic, Borg, cloud backups, and app-specific exports protect data, but none creates a small-owner-friendly manifest explaining what was backed up and how to test recovery for business records.
smallest_useful_product: Local CLI that packages configured export files, hashes and encrypts them, writes a plain-language restore manifest, verifies a target copy, and runs a scheduled dry-read. Non-goals: hosted backup storage, database administration, or vendor-specific restore automation.
success_measure: A pilot owner can locate and verify a complete recent recovery pack in under ten minutes, and scheduled verification fails loudly within one run when the target is unavailable.
monetization: one-time — backups should not force a new cloud subscription and the core task is local ownership.
constraints: Use authenticated encryption and OS keychain/passphrase support; never upload without an explicit target; document that verification is not a full application restore.
why_distinct: It turns disparate exports into a tested recovery handoff, rather than becoming another backup provider.

title: Stock Label Run
user: Small shops and makers who receive stock and need a local, repeatable way to turn a purchase list into correct barcode labels and a print receipt.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A local-first barcode tool creator reports that small businesses and sellers face expensive subscriptions or awkward tools when printing bulk inventory labels.
A Grocy user requests that stock-entry label-print webhooks include product details and the stock-entry object during purchase, showing the handoff from receiving to labeling is incomplete.

recurrence: Current 2025–2026 evidence points to the same receiving-time workflow: label creation must retain item and stock-entry context without an enterprise label suite.
current_workaround: Copy product names into label templates, create barcodes one at a time, or pay for BarTender-class software.
incumbents_and_gap: BarTender, ZebraDesigner, Sortly, and inventory suites are capable but costly or broad; small receiving runs need a local CSV-to-label workflow with a proof of what printed.
smallest_useful_product: Offline PWA that imports a CSV, validates SKU/barcode values, lays out label sheets, prints browser/PDF labels, and saves a printable run receipt. Non-goals: barcode allocation authority, POS, inventory database, or printer-driver management.
success_measure: A pilot user prints a 50-item receiving run with zero manual retyping and reconciles every printed label to an imported SKU in under 15 minutes.
monetization: one-time — label generation is a local utility and print volumes should not create a monthly tax.
constraints: Support only documented barcode symbologies and checksum validation; preserve CSV locally; do not claim marketplace-specific label compliance without test fixtures.
why_distinct: The differentiator is receiving-run traceability, not another online barcode generator.

title: Export Map
user: Owners of tiny businesses who need a dependable, accountant-friendly export of admin records without discovering incompatible CSV fields at handoff time.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A small-business administrative-app validation request names invoicing, purchases, inventory, and expense tracking as the routine workload it aims to simplify.
A self-hosted Invoice Ninja user cannot make a usable CSV export because delimiter and numeric-field formatting are incompatible with the intended downstream use.

recurrence: Administrative records span several categories, while a concrete 2025 export request shows that a nominal CSV export is not reliably handoff-ready.
current_workaround: Open CSV in a spreadsheet, fix delimiters and decimal columns by hand, then email a version whose transformations are undocumented.
incumbents_and_gap: QuickBooks, Zoho, Invoice Ninja, and spreadsheets export data, but tiny businesses need a neutral local preflight that validates an export against the recipient's declared column and locale requirements.
smallest_useful_product: Offline CSV preflight tool with saved recipient profiles, delimiter/decimal/date checks, required-column mapping, visible transformations, and a handoff manifest. Non-goals: bookkeeping, direct accounting integrations, data warehousing, or automatic tax categorization.
success_measure: At least 90% of pilot exports pass the receiving accountant's import on the first attempt, with every changed field represented in the manifest.
monetization: one-time — local export hygiene is a periodic handoff need and benefits from no third-party data retention.
constraints: Process files in-browser; preserve originals; locale conversion must be explicit and reversible; never infer tax/accounting semantics from ambiguous columns.
why_distinct: It validates the handoff boundary between existing tools instead of cloning an accounting system.
